tips_en: Start with the DataFlow-Harness paper (Paper 1) as it has the most immediate practical value: its 93.3% pass rate and 72.5% cost reduction on a concrete 12-task benchmark make the contributions easy to evaluate, and the 'NL2Pipeline gap' framing is broadly relevant to anyone building LLM agents. Then read ReferTrack (Paper 2) if you work on embodied AI—the 'referring-then-tracking' paradigm with discrete bounding-box grounding is a clean and generalizable idea worth understanding. Paper 3 (ProVisE) is best read last as a meta-evaluation piece; interestingly, it connects to Paper 1 through the theme of structured/synthesized benchmarks and to Paper 2 by offering an alternative evaluation protocol for spatial reasoning tasks.
tips_zh: 建议优先阅读 DataFlow-Harness（论文1），其实用价值最直接：在12个任务基准上达到93.3%的通过率并将成本降低72.5%，贡献易于评估，且'NL2Pipeline gap'的框架对所有构建LLM智能体的研究者都相关。如果你从事具身智能方向，可以接着读 ReferTrack（论文2），其'先指代再跟踪'的范式利用离散的边界框作为推理锚点，思路清晰且可推广。论文3（ProVisE）建议最后阅读，作为元评测类研究，它与论文1都涉及结构化/合成基准的设计思想，与论文2则在空间推理评估方法上形成有趣的对比。
